item.title: Rethinking Agentic Model Orchestration for Time Series Forecasting
item.description: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) perform unevenly across forecasting tasks. Recent work uses agentic model orchestration (AMO) to select or combine TSFMs, often outperforming individual forecasters. Yet these gains may reflect stronger or more complementary candidates rather than better orchestration. To disentangle these effects, we introduce FairAMO, a controlled evaluation protocol with frozen candidate forecasts. item.description: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes a system that improves not only its behavior but also the process by which it improves. item.title: Accept or Repair: Preserving Passage-Supported Answers in Contrastive Decoding
item.description: Large language models often answer from knowledge learned during training, even when a provided passage contradicts that knowledge. To address this problem, contrastive decoding contrasts the predictions under the full and a modified prompt at every token, but it also alters correct answers that the passage supports. We show that checking answers against the passage removes this trade-off. Based on this observation, we propose Accept-or-Repair (AoR), a training-free procedure. item.description: Existing sequential recommenders usually allocate a fixed computational budget to every item in a user's interaction history, regardless of the item's contribution to the final prediction. item.description: Video world models predict future frames from past frames and actions. They generate in the latent space of a video autoencoder, whose compression sets their cost per frame and how long each action waits to take effect. item.description: Adaptive experiments use bandit algorithms to favor interventions with higher expected rewards. item.description: World models turn visual representations into predictions and actions. item.description: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics.
